title: Operators and transformations
text: RG describes transformation pipeline operator primitives, pair coordinate reference systems. EPSG codes core Minimal context used ; compose steps : Chain operators |. Give operator key=value arguments (example utm zone=32, helmert x=-87 y=-96 z=-120, lcc lat_1=33 lat_2=45). Choose ellipsoid ellps= (example ellps=GRS80, ellps=intl); many operators default GRS80. Reverse single step trailing inv, reverse whole pipeline geod_apply(..., inv = TRUE). full set registered names:
code: geod_validate("gis:in | utm zone=32 | gis:out") #> [1] TRUE geod_ops() #>  [1] "adapt"       "addone"      "axisswap"    "btmerc"      "butm"        #>  [6] "cart"        "curvature"   "deflection"  "deformation" "dm"          #> [11] "dms"         "enu:in"      "enu:out"     "geo:in"      "geo:out"     #> [16] "geodesic"    "gis:in"      "gis:out"     "gravity"     "gridshift"   #> [21] "helmert"     "laea"        "latitude"    "latlon"      "latlong"     #> [26] "lcc"         "longlat"     "lonlat"      "merc"        "molodensky"  #> [31] "neu:in"      "neu:out"     "noop"        "omerc"       "permtide"    #> [36] "pipeline"    "pop"         "push"        "somerc"      "stack"       #> [41] "tmerc"       "unitconvert" "utm"         "webmerc"

title: Operators and transformations
text: RG supports focused set high-quality projections. Geographic input bracketed gis:(gis:geographic output).
code: # A few projections for Copenhagen (12 E, 55 N) projections <- c(   "utm zone=32",   "merc",   "webmerc",   "lcc lat_0=52 lat_1=33 lat_2=45",   "laea lat_0=52 lon_0=10" ) t(vapply(projections, function(p) {   r <- geod_apply(paste("gis:in |", p), x = 12, y = 55)   c(x = r$x, y = r$y) }, numeric(2))) #>                                        x         y #> utm zone=32                     691875.6 6098907.8 #> merc                           1335833.9 7326837.7 #> webmerc                        1335833.9 7361866.1 #> lcc lat_0=52 lat_1=33 lat_2=45  794682.6  396334.1 #> laea lat_0=52 lon_0=10          128020.4  335613.6

title: Operators and transformations
text: operators move coordinates datums reference frames. classic datum shift built going cartesian space, applying Helmert transform, coming back: 2-D caveat. rgeodesy currently passes two coordinates per point (x, y). cart, helmert deformation intrinsically three-dimensional need height round-trip faithfully, datum transforms yet fully usable 2-D interface. Projections 2-D operators unaffected.
code: geod_validate("geo:in | cart | helmert x=-87 y=-96 z=-120 | cart inv ellps=intl | geo:out") #> [1] TRUE

title: Operators and transformations
text: RG builds pipelines | separator; need name pipeline operator . Compiling bare pipeline recurses without bound upstream crash R session, rgeodesy refuses clear message:

title: R Interface to Rust Geodesy
code: library(rgeodesy)  # Geographic (lon, lat) in degrees -> UTM zone 55 south (easting, northing). geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = c(147.3, 147.5), y = c(-42.9, -42.8)) #> $x #> [1] 524492.1 540886.1 #> $y #> [1] 5250246 5261273  # The same thing as a two-column matrix. geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = c(147.3, 147.5), y = c(-42.9, -42.8)) #>             x       y #> [1,] 524492.1 5250246 #> [2,] 540886.1 5261273  # Inverse: projected -> geographic (set inv = TRUE on the forward pipeline). m <- geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9) geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = m[, "x"], y = m[, "y"], inv = TRUE) #> $x #> [1] 147.3 #> $y #> [1] -42.9

title: Apply a Rust Geodesy pipeline to coordinate vectors — geod_apply
text: Compiles pipeline applies , vectorised, coordinate pairs. Coordinates follow Rust Geodesy conventions: geographic data must bracketed adaptor operator (gis:/gis:(lon, lat) degrees, geo:/geo:(lat, lon)), RG works internally radians.

title: Apply a Rust Geodesy pipeline to coordinate vectors — geod_apply

title: Apply a Rust Geodesy pipeline to coordinate vectors — geod_apply
text: op_str Character scalar. Rust Geodesy pipeline string, e.g. "gis:| utm zone=32". x Numeric vector. First coordinate (longitude/easting GIS convention). y Numeric vector. Second coordinate (latitude/northing). Must length x. inv Logical scalar. Run inverse operation. Default FALSE.

title: Apply a Rust Geodesy pipeline to coordinate vectors — geod_apply
text: named list numeric elements x y, length input.

title: Apply a Rust Geodesy pipeline to coordinate vectors — geod_apply
code: # Geographic (lon, lat) in degrees -> UTM zone 55 south (easting, northing) geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = c(147.3, 147.5), y = c(-42.9, -42.8)) #> $x #> [1] 524492.1 540886.1 #>  #> $y #> [1] 5250246 5261273 #>   # Round trip: forward then inverse recovers the input fwd <- geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9) geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = fwd$x, y = fwd$y, inv = TRUE) #> $x #> [1] 147.3 #>  #> $y #> [1] -42.9 #>   # Multi-step pipeline: geographic in, northing-easting-up out geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=32 | neu:out", x = c(12, 18), y = c(55, 59)) #> $x #> [1] 6098908 6574904 #>  #> $y #> [1]  691875.6 1016066.6 #>
